thread:
matt: Heads up — saw a 7-12% p50/p99 host-side CPU bump after the kernel-selector rollout on edge hosts. Perf numbers from the nightly run attached.

perf-bot: benchmark summary:
- host_parse_cpu_ms: baseline=1.9 -> post=2.1 (+10.5%)
- p99 latency: 48ms -> 54ms
- smallwrite_count/request: 3 -> 7

anya: Ugh. Is this host parsing (tokenization) or the kernel handoff? Any flamegraphs?

kevin: Uploaded a quick flamegraph snippet: 
```
host_parse -> utf8_normalize (30%) -> tokenize (45%) -> grpc_writev_wait (10%) -> kvcache_lookup (5%)
```
Looks like tokenize + smallwrite stalls. Also seeing increased syscall time spread due to extra writev calls.

sam: I can repro locally with the replay harness. Replaying a mixed short-chat workload shows more smallwrite syscalls per request (avg 3 -> 7). That bumps HTTP/2 + HPACK cost and increases grpc framing overhead.

kevin: The kernel-selector change lowered GPU-side batch-sizing for short sequences to shave latency. Side effect: more host fragmentation (smaller groups) and more frequent preproc I/O. We traded GPU batch latency for host I/O pressure.

anya: Any evidence KV cache is involved? Could fragmentation increase KV churn/hot shard thrash?

kevin: kvcache telemetry on the impacted hosts shows miss_rate rise from ~4% -> ~8% for short-seq workloads. Hot-shard counters spike when small requests dominate. Correlates with increased kvcache lookups in the flamegraph.

matt: TL;DR: selector tweak -> smaller host batches -> more tokenization churn + extra small writev calls -> grpc/http2 overhead + KV thrash -> net host CPU up and tail latency up.

anya: Proposed mitigations (short list):
- Revert kernel-selector tweak for canary hosts OR roll it back fully if needed
- Coalesce tokenization output on the host proxy into fewer writev calls (bundle small chunks)
- Add a min_host_batch_size knob to selector heuristics (so GPU heuristics don't collapse host-side batching)
- Experiment with KV prefetch for very short requests to reduce miss penalty

kevin: Quick local patch: coalesce frames in proxy send path and aggregate token chunks before writev. Microbench numbers: host_parse_cpu_ms -6%, p99 tail -7% in replay. No observable change to GPU-side throughput in my run.

sam: Good. Any regression risk? Does coalescing change streaming semantics for consumers (latency for first token)?

kevin: Coalesce only merges adjacent small chunks into a single writev while preserving ordering and initial flush for first-token; first-byte latency unchanged. Implementation note: only applies when seq_len < threshold and total bytes < X.

matt: Plan of action:
1) Canary revert selector on 5% of hosts tomorrow AM (low blast radius)
2) Roll the proxy coalesce patch to canary (kevin)
3) Add min_host_batch_size config to selector and enable on canary (anya)
4) Launch KV prefetch experiment for short-seq traffic (sam)

ci-bot: Ticket created: INFR-4284. PR opened: https://git/repo/pull/6142 (placeholder).

anya: I'll take owner of the selector flag and coordinate canary schedule with infra. Kevin, please open the coalesce PR with perf artifacts and the flamegraph in the description.

kevin: Will open PR in ~30m with benchmark results and a small unit test for writev coalescing. Linking here when done. :thumbsup:

matt: Thanks all — please post updates in this thread. :eyes:
